Answer: A
Reason: The lateral view (Figure 1b) demonstrates a distinct, curvilinear calcification outlining the inferior and anterior border of the cardiac silhouette at the apex, which is the pathognomonic radiographic appearance of a calcified left ventricular aneurysm. This finding distinguishes it from pericardial calcification (which typically outlines the entire heart or AV grooves) or valvular/annular calcifications (which are located more centrally or superiorly).
